title: verifier.science context
description: The context object of a `science` request. SPEC.md section 3.1. The `resolver` field is the injected dependency of SPEC.md section 5: the profile never reaches the network itself, it asks a named resolver, and the only resolver a shipped build registers is the offline one.

rubric.description: Rubric keys the candidate must address, each with a source. The key is the identifier a verdict reports (SPEC.md section 6 permits rubric keys in evidence); `pattern` overrides how the key is looked for in the candidate. May be empty.

pattern.description: Regular expression located in the candidate. Defaults to the literal key. Matched case-insensitively.

description.description: Human-readable. Never parsed; never enters evidence.

resolver.description: Which citation resolver to use. `inline` resolves only from `sources` in this same request and therefore cannot touch the network — it is what every test and every golden case uses. `live` is registered only by a build that has explicitly installed the live resolver (profiles/science_live.py); a build that has not exits non-zero rather than silently degrading, because a resolver that resolves nothing would turn every citation into science.citation_unresolved.

sources.description: Fixture source records for the `inline` resolver, keyed by citation key. `numbers` is the set of figures the source supports, which is what number traceability is checked against.
